Shaw 2025; Pickerel 2024c). 2.6.3 Imports/Exports of Polysilicon PV wafer production has not occurred in the United States since 2015, so there was probably no significant U.S. polysilicon importation for PV in 2024 (although this is difficult to see explicitly in the trade data).29 Of the wafer capacity shown in Figure 19, Corning (which is projected to begin production in 2025) is expected to use U.S. polysilicon, and Qcells announced it would secure polysilicon for domestic wafer manufacturing from OCI Holdings’ factory in Malaysia (see Section 2.6.2) (Samora 2025). As shown in Figure 24, the largest potential source of imported polysilicon is China, although U.S. PV wafer manufacturers would generally have less access to Chinese polysilicon because of trade restrictions. Polysilicon is also available from at least two suppliers in other countries: OCI in Malaysia, with 28 GW -equivalent, and Wacker in Germany, with 38 GW -equivalent dc dc (BNEF 2025b). 28 Despite its development and commercialization in the United States, effective January 2025, all global FBR capacity was within China, controlled by GGL Poly (BNEF 2025b). 29 From 2014 to 2024, approximately 2 kilotons (kt) of 99.99% pure silicon (HTS code 2804.61.0000) were imported into the United States per year, mostly from Germany, Taiwan, and Japan, with an average price of $60/kg—suggesting these imports were for semiconductors. 35 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 24. Global polysilicon capacity by country and production for PV, 2013–2024. Source: (PV Tech Research 2025) As shown in Figure 25, the United States exported approximately 37 kt ($1.1 billion) of silicon with 4N purity or greater in 2024, down 5% year over year. Silicon at this level of purity can be used for a variety of applications, including PV and semiconductors. Approximately 21 kt (58%) went to Vietnam and Malaysia, the most probable locations for PV-related sales because of the growing amount of PV wafer manufacturing in those countries; the threefold growth in exports to those countries roughly coincides with their ramp-up in wafer manufacturing. PV Tech reported (PV Tech Research 2025) that the United States produced 11 kt of polysilicon for PV in 2024, or more than half of the amount 4N purity or greater silicon that went to Vietnam and Malaysia. All or most of this production was for export in 2024, because there was no U.S. PV wafer production. Given U.S. restrictions on Chinese polysilicon due to the UFLPA, which drove wafer manufacturing capacity in Southeast Asia, U.S. polysilicon may have been exported and eventually returned to the United States within PV cells and modules. There was greater than 30 GW of PV wafer capacity in Malaysia and Vietnam in 2024 and 2 GW of wafer capacity in dc dc Turkey by a company named Kalyon (BNEF 2025b). South Korea, Japan, and Germany have minimal PV wafer capacity but are very active in the semiconductor industry. 36 This report is available at no cost
